The user is advised not to adjust the wiring harness components without authorization. •Set laser collimated beam There is a laser beam in the experimental shed, which coincides with the X-beam trace and is used as the basis for collimating the ionization chamber and the sample. Accurate. Use X-ray sensitive paper to expose X-rays at two points, and determine the direction of the laser beam through the spatial positions of the two spots. When the sample is <5mm, or there is a special sample cell, you can ask the person on duty to calibrate the laser collimated beam to avoid the spot position being different from the sample. If the deviation is too large, the laser beam direction must not be changed without permission. 2) Adjust the detuning of monochromatic light •Why should we adjust the detuning degree? The monochromatic (monoenergetic) X-beam used in the experiment contains high-order harmonic components. The high-order components generate background noise and reduce Get the quality of your data. Fine-tuning the detuning (parallelism) of the twin crystals in the monochromator can effectively suppress higher harmonics in the beam. Portion. However, excessive detuning causes too much fundamental wave intensity loss, which is undesirable. For different experiments, set up appropriate The appropriate degree of detuning is important for improving the quality of spectrum acquisition. 3) Select the working gas ratio of the ionization chamber •Why it is necessary to change the gas ratio In this transmission XAFS experimental system, two flow-type ionization chambers are used to detect the X-ray intensity before and after the sample. The size of the chamber's absorption of X-rays is related to the type of working gas and the energy of X-rays. From theoretical analysis, it can be known that the front ionization chamber absorbs When the absorption is 20% and the post-ionization chamber absorption is more than 80%, the signal-to-noise ratio of the data obtained in the experiment is the highest. Simultaneous front and rear ionization chamber work The higher the gas consistency, the better it is to eliminate the glitch caused by the fluctuation of the light source and the monochromator on the spectrum data. influence. When changing the energy range of the monochromator during the experiment, it is necessary to change the ratio of the working gas or use a different length of ionization chamber to keep the absorption rate and gas type of the front and rear ionization chambers consistent. •Operation This site is equipped with three lengths of ionization chambers: 5cm, 17cm, and 31cm, as well as pure nitrogen and pure argon. The ratio of nitrogen to argon is 75:25. Five different ratios of working gas: 50:50 and 25:75. Figure 4 shows the results of different lengths under 20% absorption. The scanning energy range applicable to the ratio of different gases in the ionization chamber. For the selection of the front ionization chamber and its working gas, please refer to this Figure. Figure 5 shows the absorption ratio and incident light energy of a 31cm long ionization chamber under five different gas ratios. The relationship curve of the post-ionization chamber gas selection can refer to this figure. 4) Sample preparation, installation and thickness adjustment •Adjust sample thickness It can be seen from theoretical calculation that when  .t is a certain value, the best signal-to-noise ratio can be obtained. From the spectrum, After.t-Fore.t is absorption. The height of the limit jump edge. The actual situation is more complicated. Due to the diverse composition of various elements in the sample, some samples cannot be analyzed. The above requirements are met, and the difference does not change monotonically with the increase of t. If the sample is too thick or too thin, the jump limit height will be decrease, the optimal value can only be found through experimentation. For thickness testing, see Part 4 of the XAFS data acquisition software. This site is equipped with a tablet press, and powder samples can also be pressed into tablets for sample preparation. For flaky samples that cannot be made into powder by spinning or sintering, the thickness should be controlled below 100m and the area should be larger than 5×10mm and must not have holes. Prepare 2 to 3 pieces for thickness adjustment. For liquid state samples, it is recommended to use a sample box. 5) Settings of data acquisition electronic system •User concerns In the data acquisition electronics system, what users need to pay attention to are the two preamplifiers placed on the lower floor of the experimental shed. (KEITHLEY 428) Magnification setting and background current adjustment. In the data acquisition system, the output current of the front and rear ionization chambers is weak The signal is amplified by the preamplifier and converted into a voltage signal and sent to the V/F converter to be converted into a pulse signal proportional to the frequency. It is then counted by the scaler and fed into the computer. The input signal range of the V/F converter is 0-10V. Then scan θ carefully near peak A to determine the peak A*, and place θ at the peak A*; 3: Scan the χ angle within a certain angle range to find the strongest diffraction position χ0, and place the sample at this position. 4: Set the 2θ detector slit to a suitable size, generally 0.2~0.5mm, add an appropriate absorption sheet in front of the detector, do a 2θ fine scan near 69 degrees, determine the peak B*, run the detector to the peak position B*, set 2θ to 69.1 degrees, and the adjustment is completed. [Note] Be sure to add an absorbing sheet when the 2θ detector slit is opened. After the above adjustment is completed, the incident X-rays, Si (004) crystal plane and the position of the detector meet the Bragg diffraction conditions.
